items.title: `uv tree`'s flags for extra/groups are weird
items.reason: Closest ongoing design discussion. It confirms the current additive/default-group semantics while questioning the broader extras/groups asymmetry; it does not report `--only-group` failing.

items.title: Add `--group`, `--only-group`, and `--only-dev` support to `uv tree`
items.reason: Introduced the distinct additive `--group` and restrictive `--only-group` interfaces.

items.title: uv tree with --only-group doesn't show full depth
items.reason: Historical `--only-group` correctness bug fixed by astral-sh/uv#12560. It concerned missing transitive dependencies, whereas this report invokes `--group`.

related.search_scope: Literal searches covered `uv tree --group`, `tree --group`, `tree group dev`, the reported group names, and dependency-group terminology. Conceptual searches covered group-only selection, filtering, defaults, all groups, and tree output across open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests. Fix-oriented inspection covered astral-sh/uv#8338, astral-sh/uv#12526, astral-sh/uv#12560, astral-sh/uv#10890, and astral-sh/uv#11224. astral-sh/uv#19976, astral-sh/uv#19327, and astral-sh/uv#19975 were ruled out because they concern depth semantics, optional-extra rendering, and dependency-group-only projects, respectively.

type_reason: Source, CLI help, documentation, and integration snapshots establish that `--group` is additive and `--only-group` is restrictive. The partial configuration does not establish a failure of `--only-group`, so this is a usage clarification unless a complete reproduction demonstrates otherwise.
summary: No existing issue tracks a matching failure of `uv tree --only-group dev`. astral-sh/uv#19973 is the closest design discussion, while astral-sh/uv#8338 establishes the intended distinction between the two flags.
draft_response: `--group` is additive: it includes the named group alongside the project's default groups. To display only `dev`, use `uv tree --only-group dev --depth 1`; `--only-group` also disables the default groups. If `airflow` still appears with that command, please provide the complete `pyproject.toml` (including `[tool.uv]` and any workspace configuration) and the full tree output so we can reproduce it.
